title: The rent went down. So did the profit.
units_note: All money figures in ₹ lakh unless marked. Costs are shown in brackets, e.g. (96.0).

brief.headline: Sales flat, rent halved, and profit fell 44%.
brief.story: Kirana Konnect distributes packaged foods and personal-care products to 1,200 kirana stores across Jaipur, delivering daily with a fleet of hired vans. In August it moved to a bigger, cheaper warehouse and cut its rent in half. Sales held steady. Profit didn't. The owner wants to know what went wrong before signing a five-year lease extension.

evidence.title: Profit & loss statement
evidence.teaser: Every cost line, July vs August

rows: Total van km in the month

body.text: All vans are GPS-tracked. The warehouse moved on 1 Aug from near Johari Bazaar to the Bagru industrial area, about 28 km west of the city.
Two loaders were hired for the larger warehouse. Drivers come with the hired vans.

evidence.title: Retailer feedback
evidence.teaser: What the kirana owners are saying

body.text: “Van used to come by 11. Now it's after 2 most days.”
“Order is always complete, no complaints there.”
Damaged or returned goods: 0.6% of sales in both months.

causes.label: Diesel prices went up
causes.feedback: Diesel moved 20 paise a litre, and the van rate (fuel included) didn't change.

causes.label: Stores are paying late
causes.feedback: Collection days were 12 in both months, and late payment doesn't hit profit anyway.

causes.label: The new warehouse is far from the stores, so every route got much longer
Drivers are padding their kilometres
causes.feedback: Vans are GPS-tracked, and km rose on every route the day the warehouse moved.

causes.label: The van operators raised their rates
Stores are ordering smaller amounts, so more trips
causes.feedback: Same 40 routes a day, same 30 stores a route.

causes.label: The snacks category is losing money

bonus.question: What should the owner do first?
options: Negotiate the van rate down to ₹8.50/km
Load the vans closer to the city again: move back, or rent a small city cross-dock, because ₹5.4L of extra driving costs more than the ₹1.5L rent saved
Let go of the two new loaders
bonus.explanation: The move saved ₹1.5L of rent and added ₹5.4L of driving. Anything that cuts the extra 56 km per route fixes the problem at its source. A lower van rate helps, but the routes would still be twice as long. Signing the 5-year lease locks the problem in.

explanation.answer: The new warehouse is 28 km from the city, so every route nearly doubled from 62 to 118 km. At ₹9.30/km that's ₹5.4L more delivery cost, against ₹1.5L of rent saved. Net, the move cost ₹3.9L, which is 93% of the ₹4.2L profit drop.
fastest_path: Open the P&L. Delivery nearly doubled (+₹5.4L) while rent fell ₹1.5L. Everything else is flat.
Open delivery operations. Same routes, same stores, but 118 km per route instead of 62, starting the day of the move.
traps: Lower rent looks like a win, but it's the reason the trucks drive further.
Fuel prices are the obvious suspect for a delivery cost jump, but diesel and the van rate didn't move.
Late deliveries in the feedback point at drivers. They're late because the trip is longer.
explanation.lesson: Saving on rent is easy to see. The cost it moves somewhere else rarely sits on the same line.
